stem: A hospital is reviewing the responsibilities of the team member who manages its infection prevention and control program. Which activity set best reflects that role?

options.A: Coordinate HAI and pathogen surveillance, monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices, support current evidence-based policies, and provide or coordinate staff education and feedback.
options.B: Provide routine bedside assignments as the primary function and become involved in infection prevention only during declared outbreaks.
options.C: Track infection rates but avoid participating in policy, staff education, or performance-improvement activities because those functions belong exclusively to unit managers.
options.D: Focus only on employee illness records and exclude patient-care infection risks and healthcare-associated infections from the program.

rationale: A is correct. CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices call for qualified personnel to manage facility infection-prevention programs. Core program activities include monitoring healthcare-associated infections and transmission, monitoring adherence to infection-prevention requirements, providing feedback, ensuring current evidence-based policies and procedures, and providing job-specific education and training. B incorrectly limits the role to outbreak response. C fragments functions that CDC treats as components of the infection-prevention program. D confuses a facility-wide infection-prevention program with occupational health alone.
educational_objective: Recognize infection-prevention program leadership as an ongoing systems role that integrates surveillance, policy implementation, performance monitoring and feedback, and healthcare-personnel education rather than functioning only during outbreaks.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; Isolation Precautions — Fundamental Elements Needed to Prevent Transmission
source_version_date: Current CDC Infection Control pages accessed 2026-08-17; core-practices page current through 2024–2026 web maintenance
source_locator: Core Practices Table — Leadership Support: assign qualified individuals trained in infection prevention and control to manage the facility IPC program. Education and Training: provide job-specific IPC education and current evidence-based written policies/procedures. Performance Monitoring and Feedback: monitor adherence to IPC practices and infection incidence, provide regular feedback, and use surveillance to detect transmission. Isolation Precautions, Surveillance for HAIs: surveillance is an essential ongoing systematic activity for identifying infections, clusters, and indications for change.
source_claim_supported: A facility infection-prevention program is managed by qualified IPC personnel and includes ongoing surveillance, evidence-based policy support, staff education, monitoring of practice adherence, feedback, and response to identified transmission risks.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, participate in quality-improvement systems, and use organizational resources to promote safe client care.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — role of infection-prevention program leadership
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw role-definition item using current CDC program components rather than relying on a generic professional-organization role description. The final answer is bounded to actual facility IPC functions—surveillance, policy, education, monitoring, and feedback—without claiming one profession must perform every task personally.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current CDC Core IPC Practices and Isolation Precautions surveillance guidance.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A combines explicit CDC program functions. B falsely restricts the role to bedside care/outbreaks. C excludes policy/education/feedback despite CDC listing them as core components. D narrows a facility IPC program to occupational health only.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; reflects ongoing systems-level IPC management.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; prevention work is continuous, not outbreak-only.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; policy, education, monitoring, and feedback are integral IPC functions.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; patient HAI and transmission surveillance are central to IPC.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A captures the integrated facility-level role without overassigning bedside or occupational-health functions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe plausible organizational role boundaries.
audit_findings.blueprint: Systems collaboration and quality/safety program work fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked whether policy 'development' should be attributed solely to the infection preventionist. The final wording says support current policies and manage/co-ordinate program functions, avoiding an unsupported exclusive-authority claim. No second answer remained.
